identity.title: Dual-wavelength ALMA Observations of Dust Rings in Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present new Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations for three protoplanetary disks in Taurus at 2.9 mm and comparisons with previous 1.3 mm data

question.value: Do dust rings in three Taurus disks appear at the same locations and widths at 1.3 and 2.9 mm, and what do disk sizes, ring widths, spectral index and optical depth imply for dust trapping and grain growth?

evidence.quote: This comparison aims to test the presence of dust traps and also provide insights for grain property changes, to better understand the role of dust substructures in planet formation process.
were taken between 2019 July 16 and July 28 (#2018.1.00614.S, PI. Long)
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: 2016.1.01164.S and 2018.1.00614.S.

bands.value: Band 3 (2.9 mm, new) and Band 6 (1.3 mm, previous)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 3 continuum SPWs at 98, 100, 112 GHz, 1.875 GHz each; 4th window for 13CO and C18O, ~0.7 km/s channels

evidence.quote: Three spectral windows were set up for continuum observations, centered at 98, 100, and 112 GHz, each with a bandwidth of 1.875 GHz.

baselines.value: Band 3: 90 m to ~8.5 km; Band 6: 21 m to 3.6 km

evidence.quote: The array was configured to span baselines from 90 m to $\sim$8.5 km with 43–45 antennas
both at an angular resolution of $\sim0.1\ensuremath{''}$ (15 au for the distance of Taurus)

sensitivity.value: RMS 12.8-16.5 uJy/beam at Band 3; 58.5-82.5 at Band 6

time_on_source.value: 66.5, 77.6, 67.3 min for DS Tau, GO Tau, DL Tau

evidence.quote: The total on-source integration time were 66.5 min, 77.6 min, and 67.3 min for DS Tau, GO Tau, and DL Tau, respectively.
were taken between 2019 July 16 and July 28
The distance for individual stars is adopted from the Gaia DR2 parallax

what.value: 1.3 mm Band 6 data, ring locations, inclinations/PAs priors

evidence.quote: identified from our previous 1.3 mm survey at 0.1$''$ resolution
Stellar mass and age are adopted from (cite: Long2019).
Spectral type is adopted from (cite: herczeg2014)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Dust evolution model with embedded planet at 33 au, alpha=1e-3, 5.8 MJup disk, 0.58 Msun star, vfrag 10 m/s

evidence.quote: We take an $\alpha$-viscosity parameter of $10^{-3}$ (independent of radius and time)
The data were calibrated by ALMA pipeline with the Common Astronomy Software Package (CASA), version 5.4.0.
Further calibration and imaging were also performed with this same version.
Bandpass and flux calibrations used observations of the quasar J0510+1800 for all executions.
a $\sim10$% flux calibration uncertainty at each wavelength would introduce a systematic offset of $\sim$0.2 in $\alpha_{\rm mm}$

self_calibration.value: Two rounds phase-only (120 s, 60 s) for GO Tau and DL Tau; not for DS Tau

evidence.quote: We performed two rounds of phase-only self-calibration with solution intervals of 120s and 60s
The Band 3 continuum images were obtained with the multi-term, multi-frequency synthesis algorithm (`mtmfs`) in `tclean` with *nterms* = 2.

weighting_robust.value: DS Tau robust=-0.5; GO Tau and DL Tau robust=0.0

evidence.quote: For DS Tau, we started with Briggs weighting with robust = -0.5 at both bands
the final images at both bands were convolved into a common beam size using the `imsmooth` task.
Both images were then convolved to reach a targeted beam size of $0.13\ensuremath{''}\times0.09\ensuremath{''}$.
The 1$\sigma$ noise levels measured in the signal-free regions are in the range of 12 to 16 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$

what.value: Parametric intensity profile forms and number of rings from the 1.3 mm analysis

evidence.quote: we adopt the same intensity profiles as (cite: Long2018)

what.value: Priors on inclination and PA centered on earlier values

evidence.quote: Priors on disk inclination and position angles are centered at what identified before (cite: Long2018) with a range of $\pm$20$\ensuremath{^\circ}$.

what.value: Disk size metric of fixed fraction of encircled flux

evidence.quote: we adopt a generic definition of size - the location where a fixed fraction of the total disk flux is encircled, as introduced by (cite: Tripathi2017).
The flaring angle is taken to be $\varphi=0.02$, the same as the value used in the DSHARP analysis

Image size, cell size, deconvolver details and masks for tclean

analysis_steps.goal: Image Band 3 continuum and match resolution to Band 6

method.value: tclean mtmfs nterms=2, self-cal for GO/DL Tau, imsmooth to common beams

evidence.quote: The Band 3 continuum images were obtained with the multi-term, multi-frequency synthesis algorithm (`mtmfs`) in `tclean` with *nterms* = 2.
For GO Tau and DL Tau, the initial images from robust = 0.0

analysis_steps.goal: Fit uv visibilities with parametric radial profiles

method.value: Galario synthetic visibilities, MCMC with emcee

evidence.quote: we generate synthetic visibilities using the *Galario* code (cite: Tazzari2018), sampled at the observed uv-space.

key_parameters.value: 100 walkers, 5000 steps, last 1000 used; grid 0.0001-4" step 0.0005"

evidence.quote: The free parameters are sampled with 100 walkers and 5000 steps for each walker.

assumptions.value: axisymmetric profiles; Gaussian inner disk for DS Tau, tapered power law for GO/DL Tau, Gaussian rings

evidence.quote: The same functional forms, including same numbers of Gaussian rings, are used for the fitting of individual disks at both wavelengths.

fitting.value: Uniform priors on logF in [6,11] Jy/sr, sigma in [0,0.2"], gamma1 [0,2], gamma2 [0,20], rc [0,0.4"], ring centers +-0.05"; peaks of marginal posteriors, 68% intervals

evidence.quote: The adopted parameters are taken as the peaks of marginal posteriors, with uncertainties given by the 68% confidence intervals

validation.value: Residual images (3-5 sigma) and binned visibility comparison

evidence.quote: Our models match the overall structures in the visibility profiles reasonably well.

method.value: radius enclosing 95% (disk) or 68% (inner disk, cut at first local minimum) of model flux

evidence.quote: we measure the effective disk size as 95% of emission encircled in the adopted model intensity profile

analysis_steps.goal: Compute spectral index, optical depth, beta

method.value: alpha from intensity profiles at two bands; tau from full Planck function with irradiated disk temperature

evidence.quote: We estimate optical depth of the dust emission using the expression of

key_parameters.value: flaring angle 0.02, Td ~15 K at 50 au

evidence.quote: corresponding to T$_{d}\sim$ 15 K and h/r = 0.06–0.08 at 50 au for our sample

assumptions.value: Td equals midplane irradiated temperature; absorption-dominated opacity

evidence.quote: The analysis above is based on an assumption that millimeter emission is dominated by absorption.

validation.value: Compared model-based and image-based alpha profiles

evidence.quote: Spectral index profiles estimated from the azimuthally averaged brightness profiles (see Figure [5](#fig:alpha)) preserve the overall morphology

analysis_steps.goal: Dust evolution modelling with pressure bump

method.value: Dust growth/fragmentation/drift model with planet-carved gap (Crida2006, Fung2014 corrections)

evidence.quote: We use the prescription from (cite: Crida2006) for an analytical shape of the gap carved by a planet

key_parameters.value: planet at 33 au, q=0.002, Rc=80 au, gamma=1, alpha=1e-3, vfrag=10 m/s, 180 size cells 1 um-2 m, 300 radial cells 1-300 au

evidence.quote: The grid for particle size has 180 cells logarithmic spaced from 1 $\mu$m to 2 m

assumptions.value: Gas-to-dust 100, 20% dust lost to drift, disk mass 5.8 MJup

evidence.quote: we assume a disk mass of 5.8 $M_{\rm{Jup}}$

validation.value: Compared model intensity profiles convolved to 0.1" with observations

evidence.quote: which are convolved with a Gaussian profile whose width is 0.1$''$ as our observations.
The data were calibrated by ALMA pipeline with the Common Astronomy Software Package (CASA), version 5.4.0.
we generate synthetic visibilities using the *Galario* code (cite: Tazzari2018)
Our fitting is then performed using *emcee v3.0.1*

used_for.value: curve_fit Gaussian ring fits in image plane

evidence.loc: Simple Gaussian fit to dust rings
evidence.quote: The fit is performed with $curve\_fit$ in SCIPY package.

DS Tau ring width sigma at 2.9 mm
DS Tau 2.9 mm ring width, power-law inner disk model

evidence.quote: $\sigma_{uv,\rm 2.9mm}= 5.4\pm0.8$ au

results_numeric.quantity: Disk-integrated alpha_mm (DS Tau, GO Tau, DL Tau)

the typical optical depth is about 0.1–0.2 for dust rings at 2.9 mm and 0.2–0.4 for dust rings at 1.3 mm

results_numeric.quantity: Inner disk radius 2.9 mm vs 1.3 mm (DS Tau)

evidence.quote: The values for $R_{\rm inner,2.9mm}$ and $R_{\rm inner,1.3mm}$ are 11.7 and 15.5 au for DS Tau

results_numeric.quantity: Model ring width from dust evolution (unconvolved)

evidence.quote: We therefore determine the ring width to be only 1.09 au at 2.9 mm and 1.29 au at 1.3 mm.

findings_qualitative.value: Same rings detected at both wavelengths at the same locations; disk outer radii consistent between wavelengths

evidence.quote: the same rings are detected at both wavelengths, with radial locations spanning from 50 to 120 au

findings_qualitative.value: Spectral index increases outward with local minima at high-contrast ring peaks

evidence.quote: The spectral index ($\alpha_{\rm mm}$) increases outward and exhibits local minima that correspond to the peaks of dust rings

claims.hypothesis: Dust traps keep disk radii the same at different wavelengths
claims.experiment: uv-plane fits at 1.3 and 2.9 mm and dust evolution model with/without pressure bump
claims.result: R95% consistent within uncertainties; model with bump gives equal radii, smooth disk gives smaller radii at long wavelength
claims.finding: Observations consistent with dust trapping setting disk size

evidence.quote: Dust emission at both wavelengths have similar outer radii in our sample of disks

claims.hypothesis: Rings are narrower at longer wavelength
claims.result: DS Tau ring tentatively narrower at 2.9 mm; others unresolved
claims.finding: Only tentative evidence; depends on function choice

evidence.quote: shows a tentatively narrower ring at 2.9 mm than at 1.3 mm based on visibility fitting with sub-beam resolution

claims.hypothesis: Rings are optically thin and host mm-sized grains
claims.experiment: Spectral index, tau and beta profiles
claims.finding: Grains in rings may have grown to mm sizes

evidence.quote: suggest that grains in the rings may have grown to millimeter sizes

why_this_data.value: Select disks with optically thin rings from the 1.3 mm survey; longer wavelength has lower optical depth

evidence.quote: we select three disks (DS Tau, GO Tau, and DL Tau) with optically thin rings identified from our previous 1.3 mm survey

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tapered power-law or Nuker inner disk for DS Tau tested; extra Gaussian ring in inner disk failed to converge

evidence.quote: Attempts at fitting with an additional Gaussian ring component in the inner disk failed to converge (after 10000 steps).

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties of GO Tau and DL Tau ring properties likely underestimated; function choice affects results; resolution washes out alpha variations

evidence.quote: uncertainties in the dust ring properties could be largely underestimated in GO Tau and DL Tau.

referee_caveats_inferred: Optical depth and beta depend on assumed low temperature (phi=0.02) and ignore scattering
Ring widths below beam size depend on parametric form
Dust evolution model tuned to only DS Tau with single alpha

data_public_as_stated.value: Project codes given; public status not explicitly stated

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: 2016.1.01164.S and 2018.1.00614.S.

missing_for_reproduction: Dust evolution code not named or released
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB (two projects, long-baseline, 3 targets)
reproducibility.score_reason: uv-fit recipe, priors and MCMC settings are well specified, but imaging details and the dust evolution code are missing and Band 6 processing is inherited.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA data are archival projects, the uv-fit recipe is mostly complete, and the main results are numeric tables (R95, ring widths).
